$comment: D-OPT-JCC-FALLTHROUGH runtime pin. `lir_peephole`'s rule R2 stops a conditional branch from materializing its FALLTHROUGH edge when that successor is already the next-laid-out block — the branch encodes one target instead of two (x86_64: 6 bytes instead of 11; arm64: one word instead of two), while the CFG keeps both edges. The failure mode is INVISIBLE to structural checks: elide the wrong edge, or let a later pass reorder blocks, and control falls into a block it never branched to with every byte in the image individually correct. So each decision here owns one bit of the exit code and every wrong-way branch sets bit 6 (64), which no correct run ever sets. Five shapes give the layout both answers — if/else (false edge = else block), if with no else (false edge = join), while (false edge leaves the loop), short-circuit && (extra blocks), for with an inner if — so BOTH arms of R2, elide and refuse, run here. Inputs are `volatile` so ConstFold cannot evaluate the branches away and the `release` arm exercises the same branches as the baseline. exit = 1|2|4|8|16|32 = 63.
